subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Instant Coffee's Surprising Story
description: A 60-second lesson on Instant Coffee's Surprising Story.

hook.text: Instant coffee was invented in 1901 by a Japanese-American chemist named Satori Kato at a world's fair.

buildup.text: Nescafé launched in 1938 after Brazil asked Nestlé to help preserve surplus beans. They freeze-dried them.

discovery.text: During WWII, the U.S. military distributed instant coffee in ration packs. Soldiers called it 'a cup of Joe.'

twist.text: Instant coffee still dominates many markets. In the UK and Australia, it outsells ground coffee.

climax.text: New freeze-dry techniques have dramatically improved quality. Some specialty brands now make premium instant.

punchline.text: Born from surplus, fueled by war, still going strong.

quiz.question: Why was Nescafé originally created?
options: To help Brazil preserve surplus coffee beans
